added_lines: in november we remember … as the month of november approaches we are reminded once again of our loved ones who have died and we remember them in a special way and pray for them in all our masses and prayers during the month. beginning on all saints day and throughout the month of november, nine masses for the dead will be celebrated between both ferrybank & slieverue. mass for deceased bishops, priests and religious sunday, 8th november 2026 bishop ger will celebrate a memorial mass for deceased bishops, priests and religious of the diocese of ossory on sunday, 8th november 2026 in st mary's cathedral, kilkenny, at 5.30 p.m. and extends an invitation to priests, religious and the lay faithful to join in prayer as we remember with gratitude all who served in ossory. all are welcome. mass of the sick and anointing of the sick the sacrament of anointing of the sick brings spiritual grace, peace, strength, comfort and healing. it can restore spiritual, emotional and physical health, if it is god’s will. any catholic or christian in serious illness, advancing age or preparing for surgery can avail of it. it can be repeated monthly or if an illness worsens. the priest lays his hands on the person and anoints their forehead and the sanctuary lamp burns in our church every hour of every day this week before the blessed sacrament in … ferrybank special intention – slieverue special remembrance – patrick & mary atkins the palms of their hands with blessed oil offering a special prayer of healing and grace. in relation to this important sacrament, starting in november, the last thursday of the month in ferrybank at 10.00am and the last friday of the month at 10.00am in slieverue, a special mass of the sick including anointing will be celebrated. for ticket. date for your diary. not to be missed - november 6th in the rhu glenn country club at 7.30pm. admission €10. relive a wonderful parish event in the rhu glenn, from 1994; the 40th anniversary of sliev erue winning the county hurling final in 1954 was captured on video and will be shown on the opening night of eigse. light refreshments will be served at the interval. deise draw 2026 the final déise draw of 2026 will take place on wednesday, october 28, and everyone at ferrybank gaa wishes the very best of luck to all club members participating. the draw, which will be broadcast live on wlr, continues to provide vital funding that helps sustain and develop gaelic games in ferrybank, an important part of c ommunity life. the club has enjoyed a few winners throughout the year and hopes that good fortune will continue in the final draw. ferrybank gaa would also like to sincerely thank all those who support the club through membership, fundraising and other initiatives. it has been a memorable year on the playing fields. the junior hurlers captured both divisional and county championsh ip honours, while the junior footballers secured the divisional title and contested the county final (on saturday). the camogie team also enjoyed outstanding success, completing a league and county championship double. the club is immensely proud of the achievements of all its players, coaches and volunteers during another successful year south kilkenny historical society lecture 100 years of the (dreaded) leaving cert friday, october 30th with speaker eoin walsh at mullinavat parish hall (opposite st. beacon's church) admission: €5, society members free. everyone living in ireland today has heard of it, if not sat, the dreaded leaving certificate. it has recently passed a milestone of 100 years of existence. but howdid it come about? and why do we still get nightmares about it as adults?

. a victory for the generations what an extraordinary few days it has been for durrow and cullohill! the celebrations following the historic victory last sunday will live long in the memories of everyone associated with the club and our two communities. and deservedly so. sixty-two years after cullohill’s great win and forty-two years since the harps was formed, the dream of winning a senior county championship has finally been realised. but amidst all the excitement and celebrations, i found myself thinking about another group of people: those who would have loved to see this day but are no longer with us. a few weeks ago, while working with priests in mayo, i was struck by how often people spoke about their county's great all-ireland victory, not simply in terms of the present generation, but of parents, grandparents and generations of supporters who had gone before them. people who followed their team through good times and bad, who dreamed of such a day but never lived to see it. i suspect there were similar thoughts in many hearts and homes around durrow and cullohill last sunday. how many former players, parents, grandparents and lifelong supporters would have given anything to witness that final whistle? some now have sons, grandsons or even great-grandsons among this extraordinary group of young men. their contribution to sunday's victory may not appear in any match report, but surely it is part of the story. as we approach november, the month when we traditionally remember our dead, there is something particularly appropriate this year about remembering those who helped build and sustain the clubs down through the generations. we inherit far more than a name or a place. we inherit traditions, loyalties, friendships and dreams. sometimes, without even realising it, we find ourselves completing something that others began long before us. this sunday's gospel reminds us of the great commandment to love god and to love our neighbour. perhaps one of the loveliest expressions of that love is the sense of community, belonging and generosity that occasions like last sunday bring to the surface. despite my camross roots, and the shock and disappointment being felt in the foothills of the sliabh blooms, seeing the joy this victory has brought to the people among whom i now live and serve has been something very special indeed. so, congratulations to every member of the harps family. enjoy this wonderful achievement. and somewhere in the celebrations, spare a thought for those who would have loved to be there. this victory belongs to them too. fr. martin christmas concert michael english, featuring durrow and cullohill parish choirs sunday 6th december 2026 in holy trinity church, durrow. doors open at 5 pm for 6 pm start. a festive evening of songs, stories, faith & inspiration tickets €30 available from both of our parish ofïces (opening times below) or through
